# f5xc_external_connector (Resource)

External Connector configuration mainly includes the following:<br>1. Tunnel connfiguration between F5 CE and external (3rd party) device<br>2. Tunnel specific parameters (IPSec, GRE)

To get more information about f5xc_external_connector, refer:

- [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.f5.com/docs-v2/api/views-external-connector)

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: External Connector with a GRE tunnel

# Replace the CE site, node, interface, and peer address with values from your environment.
resource "f5xc_external_connector" "example" {
  name        = "example-external-connector"
  namespace   = "system"
  description = "GRE external connector for an existing CE site"

  labels = {
    env  = "example"
    team = "network-security"
  }

  annotations = {
    owner = "platform-team"
  }

  ce_site_reference = {
    name      = "example-ce-site"
    namespace = "system"
  }

  connection_type_choice = {
    gre = {
      gre_parameters = {
        peer_ip_address = {
          addr = "203.0.113.10"
        }

        tunnel_mtu = 1370
        tunnel_eps = [{
          node             = "example-ce-node"
          interface        = "example-ce-interface"
          local_tunnel_ip  = "169.254.3.1/30"
          remote_tunnel_ip = "169.254.3.2/30"
        }]

        tunnel_source_vn_choice = {
          site_local_inside_network = true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```terraform
# Example: External Connector with an IPSec tunnel using F5 XC system-shared IKE profiles

# F5 XC predefined IKE Phase 1 and Phase 2 profiles reside in the "shared" namespace under
# tenant "ves-io". When referencing them from a non-shared namespace (such as "system"),
# you must explicitly set tenant = "ves-io".
resource "f5xc_external_connector" "ipsec_example" {
  name        = "example-ipsec-external-connector"
  namespace   = "system"
  description = "IPSec external connector for an existing CE site"

  ce_site_reference = {
    name      = "example-ce-site"
    namespace = "system"
  }

  connection_type_choice = {
    ipsec = {
      ike_parameters = {
        ike_phase1_profile = {
          name      = "ves-io-f5-ike-phase1-default-profile"
          namespace = "shared"
          tenant    = "ves-io"
        }

        ike_phase2_profile = {
          name      = "ves-io-f5-ike-phase2-default-profile"
          namespace = "shared"
          tenant    = "ves-io"
        }

        mode_choice = {
          initiator = true
        }

        dpd_choice = {
          dpd_keep_alive_timer = {
            timeout = 3
          }
        }

        local_ike_id_choice = {
          use_default_local_ike_id = true
        }

        remote_ike_id_choice = {
          use_default_remote_ike_id = true
        }
      }

      ipsec_tunnel_parameters = {
        peer_ip_address = {
          addr = "203.0.113.10"
        }

        psk        = "<pre-shared-key>"
        tunnel_mtu = 1370

        tunnel_eps = [{
          node             = "example-ce-node"
          interface        = "example-ce-interface"
          local_tunnel_ip  = "169.254.3.1/30"
          remote_tunnel_ip = "169.254.3.2/30"
        }]

        tunnel_source_vn_choice = {
          site_local_inside_network = true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an `import` block to import this resource by ID.

> **Note:** Replace placeholder values (for example, `<namespace>`, `<name>`) with actual values.

#### Command-Line Import

Use the following `command` to import this resource from the command line:

```shell
terraform import f5xc_external_connector.example <namespace>/<name>
```

#### HCL Import Block

Use the following `hcl` block to import this resource during `plan` or `apply`:

```hcl
import {
	id = "<namespace>/<name>"
	to = f5xc_external_connector.example
}
```
